# The Size Effect {#sec-size-replication}

[]{#sec-size}

We follow Chapter 9 of Bali, Engle, and Murray (2016),
*Empirical Asset Pricing*. We compare monthly and June-based size, then
examine how each relates to subsequent stock returns. Formation months
run from June 1963 through November 2012.

## Calculating Market Capitalization {#reconstruct-the-published-sample}

The book was published in 2016, well before CRSP's CIZ format. This
replication uses the legacy (SIZ) monthly stock and names files, not the
CIZ files used in the earlier chapters. Our legacy snapshot is newer
than the authors' original data, even though we use the same sample dates.
See the [WRDS table list](data.qmd#data-vintages) for the embedded update dates.

Use the share code in force at the end of each month. Keep share codes 10 and 11, without adding an exchange screen.
The book's measure uses the absolute alternate price and shares outstanding.
CRSP records shares in thousands; dividing their product by 1,000 gives
market capitalization in millions of dollars. Treat zeros as missing.

```{python}
import polars as pl
from era_pl import load_parquet

first = pl.date(1963, 6, 1)
last = pl.date(2012, 11, 1)

prices = (
    load_parquet("msf", "crsp")
    .filter(pl.col("date").is_between(pl.date(1962, 12, 1), pl.date(2012, 12, 31)))
    .with_columns(
        month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start(),
        cap=pl.when((pl.col("altprc") != 0) & (pl.col("shrout") > 0))
        .then((pl.col("altprc") * pl.col("shrout")).abs() / 1000),
    )
    .select("permno", "month", "cap")
)
names = (
    load_parquet("msenames", "crsp")
    .select("permno", "namedt", "nameendt", "shrcd", "exchcd")
    .sort("namedt")
)
stock_months = (
    prices
    .with_columns(month_end=pl.col("month").dt.month_end())
    .sort("month_end")
    .join_asof(
        names, left_on="month_end", right_on="namedt",
        by="permno", check_sortedness=False,
    )
    .with_columns(
        common=(pl.col("month_end").is_between("namedt", "nameendt")
                & pl.col("shrcd").is_in([10, 11])).fill_null(False),
        exchcd=pl.when(pl.col("month_end").is_between("namedt", "nameendt"))
        .then(pl.col("exchcd")),
    )
    .select("permno", "month", "common", "exchcd", "cap")
)
```

For the annual measure, join each stock to its capitalization at the
most recent June. A stock without a record for that particular June
has no annual value. We do not carry forward an older June observation.

```{python}
june_caps = (
    prices
    .filter(pl.col("month").dt.month() == 6)
    .select("permno", june="month", cap_june="cap")
)
june_year = pl.col("month").dt.year() - (pl.col("month").dt.month() < 6)
stock_months = (
    stock_months
    .with_columns(june=pl.date(june_year, 6, 1))
    .join(june_caps, on=["permno", "june"], how="left", validate="m:1")
    .drop("june")
)
```

[]{#compare-four-measures-of-size-and-their-logs}

Convert nominal market capitalization to December 2012 dollars using
the [BLS CPI-U, not seasonally adjusted](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCNS).
Use the CPI for the current observation month for both the monthly and
the June-based measures, as in the book.

```{python}
cpi = pl.read_csv("data/cpi-aucns.csv", try_parse_dates=True).rename(
    {"observation_date": "month", "CPIAUCNS": "cpi"}
)
cpi_2012 = cpi.filter(pl.col("month") == pl.date(2012, 12, 1))["cpi"].item()

all_sizes = (
    stock_months
    .join(cpi.lazy(), on="month", how="left", validate="m:1")
    .with_columns(
        cap_real=pl.col("cap") * cpi_2012 / pl.col("cpi"),
        cap_june_real=pl.col("cap_june") * cpi_2012 / pl.col("cpi"),
    )
    .drop("cpi")
    .with_columns(
        pl.col(var).log().alias(f"log_{var}")
        for var in ["cap", "cap_real", "cap_june", "cap_june_real"]
    )
    .collect()
)
sizes = all_sizes.filter(
    pl.col("common"), pl.col("month").is_between(first, last)
)
```

The optional export, `eap.sizes`, includes the earlier December market
equity needed for book-to-market and December 2012 for the annual
teaching sample. It records common-stock eligibility separately so the
prior December price remains available when a stock's share code changes.

{{< include _write-eap.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| include: false

assert sizes["month"].n_unique() == 594
assert all_sizes.select(pl.struct("permno", "month").n_unique()).item() == all_sizes.height
assert all_sizes.filter(pl.col("cap").is_not_null())["cap_real"].null_count() == 0
if os.environ.get("EAP_WRITE_SIZES") == "1":
    write_eap_table(all_sizes, "sizes")
```

## Summary Statistics

The mean of the monthly medians describes the middle stock in a typical
month. It is not a median calculated once on the pooled stock-month data.

```{python}
from _bem_monthly import mean_cross_sections

stats = mean_cross_sections(sizes, {
    "cap": "MktCap", "cap_real": "MktCap CPI",
    "log_cap": "Size", "log_cap_real": "Size CPI",
    "cap_june": "MktCap FF", "cap_june_real": "MktCap FF CPI",
    "log_cap_june": "Size FF", "log_cap_june_real": "Size FF CPI",
})
```

{{< include _show-table.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-summary
#| tbl-cap: Monthly summary statistics for size (BEM Table 9.1)
#| echo: false

show_table(stats)
```

The published nominal market capitalization has a monthly mean of $1,101
million and an average monthly median of $107 million. The much larger
mean reflects the concentration of market capitalization in a few stocks.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem9-concentration
#| fig-cap: Share of market capitalization held by the largest stocks (BEM Figure 9.1)
#| echo: false

from plotnine_polars import aes

caps = sizes.filter(pl.col("cap").is_not_null()).sort(
    ["month", "cap", "permno"], descending=[False, True, False],
)
fractions = [.01, .05, .10, .25]
shares = (
    caps.with_columns(rank=pl.col("cap").cum_count().over("month"))
    .group_by("month").agg(
        (pl.col("cap").filter(pl.col("rank") <= (p * pl.len()).round()).sum()
         / pl.col("cap").sum()).alias(f"Largest {p:.0%}")
        for p in fractions
    )
    .sort("month")
)
(
    shares.unpivot(index="month", variable_name="group", value_name="share")
    .with_columns(pl.col("group").cast(pl.Enum([f"Largest {p:.0%}" for p in fractions])))
    .ggplot(aes(x="month", y="share", color="group"))
    .geom_line()
    .scale_x_date(date_breaks="10 years", date_labels="%Y")
    .scale_y_continuous(limits=(0, 1), labels=lambda values: [f"{value:.0%}" for value in values])
    .scale_color_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2")
    .labs(x="Month", y="Share of market capitalization", color="")
    .theme_minimal()
    .add_theme(figure_size=(8, 4), legend_position="top")
)
```

## Correlations {#correlation-and-persistence}

Join the size measures to the twelve-month daily beta from
[Chapter 8](beta-replication.qmd). We take the mean of the monthly
cross-sectional correlations. Below the diagonal are Pearson
correlations on winsorized observations, and above it are Spearman
correlations on the original ranks.

```{python}
from _bem_monthly import correlation_matrix, monthly_panel, period_correlations, persistence

panel = monthly_panel(sizes, first, last)
measures = {"cap": "MktCap", "log_cap": "Size", "cap_june": "MktCap FF",
            "log_cap_june": "Size FF", "beta": "Beta"}
corr = period_correlations(panel, measures, "month").select(pl.exclude("month").mean())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-correlations
#| tbl-cap: Cross-sectional correlations for size and beta (BEM Table 9.2)
#| echo: false
show_table(correlation_matrix(corr.row(0, named=True), measures))
```

## Persistence

For persistence, match the same stock at a fixed calendar lag, then
winsorize both sides within the matched sample at the 0.5th and 99.5th
percentiles.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-persistence
#| tbl-cap: Persistence of nominal size measures (BEM Table 9.3)
#| echo: false
size_measures = {k: v for k, v in measures.items() if k != "beta"}
show_table(persistence(panel, size_measures, [1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 120]))
```

## Size and Stock Returns {#size-and-future-returns}

### Univariate Portfolio Analysis

Sort stocks at the end of month $t$ and measure their excess returns in
$t+1$, using the [Chapter 7](crsp-replication.qmd) delisting rules. First
use NYSE stocks to calculate the breakpoints, then use all eligible
stocks. In both cases, assign stocks from the full eligible sample.
For the June-based sort, the value weights use June capitalization, as
in BEM. Returns and CAPM alphas are in percent per month. The
$t$-statistics use six Newey–West lags.

```{python}
from _bem_monthly import bivariate_months, bivariate_panel, fama_macbeth_table, univariate_panel

def size_deciles(nyse):
    return pl.concat([
        univariate_panel(
            panel.with_columns(total=pl.col(cap).sum().over("month")), cap, nyse,
            [
                pl.col(cap).mean().alias("Market cap"),
                pl.col(real).mean().alias("Market cap, 2012 dollars"),
                (100 * pl.col(cap).sum() / pl.col("total").first()).alias("% of market cap"),
                (100 * (pl.col("exchcd") == 1).fill_null(False).mean()).alias("% NYSE"),
                pl.len().alias("Stocks"), pl.col("beta").mean().alias("Beta"),
            ],
            weight=cap,
        ).with_columns(pl.lit(label).alias("Sort"))
        for cap, real, label in [
            ("cap", "cap_real", "Monthly"), ("cap_june", "cap_june_real", "June"),
        ]
    ]).select("Sort", pl.exclude("Sort"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-deciles
#| tbl-cap: Size deciles using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.4)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_deciles(nyse=True))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-deciles
#| tbl-cap: Size deciles using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.5)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_deciles(nyse=False))
```

With NYSE breakpoints, the equal-weighted large-minus-small spread for
monthly size is −0.49% per month, as in BEM. Using all-stock breakpoints
increases its magnitude to −1.54%, compared with −1.59% in the book.
The difference comes primarily from the smallest decile.

### Bivariate Portfolio Analysis {#sort-on-beta-and-size}

For a dependent sort, form beta quintiles first and compute size
breakpoints within each beta quintile. For an independent sort, compute
beta and size breakpoints separately across the reference universe.
The rows are size quintiles and the columns are beta quintiles.
Average portfolios give each constituent portfolio equal weight each month.

```{python}
def size_quintiles(nyse, dependent):
    monthly = bivariate_months(panel, "beta", "cap", nyse=nyse, dependent=dependent)
    return pl.concat([
        bivariate_panel(monthly, weight, independent=not dependent)
        .with_columns(pl.lit(weight).alias("Weights"))
        for weight in ("EW", "VW")
    ]).select("Weights", pl.exclude("Weights")).rename({"Target": "Size"})
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-dependent
#| tbl-cap: Dependent beta and size sorts using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.6)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_quintiles(nyse=True, dependent=True))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-dependent
#| tbl-cap: Dependent beta and size sorts using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.7)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_quintiles(nyse=False, dependent=True))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-independent
#| tbl-cap: Independent beta and size sorts using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.8)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_quintiles(nyse=True, dependent=False))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-independent
#| tbl-cap: Independent beta and size sorts using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.9)
#| echo: false
show_table(size_quintiles(nyse=False, dependent=False))
```

### Fama–MacBeth Regression Analysis {#famamacbeth-regressions}

Regress the next month's excess return on log market capitalization,
with and without beta. Winsorize the regressors by month at the 0.5th
and 99.5th percentiles. Apply six Newey–West lags to the time series
of monthly coefficient estimates.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-fm
#| tbl-cap: Fama–MacBeth regressions of returns on size (BEM Table 9.10)
#| echo: false

specifications = [
    ["log_cap"], ["log_cap", "beta"], ["log_cap_june"], ["log_cap_june", "beta"],
]
show_table(fama_macbeth_table(panel, specifications,
                             {"log_cap": "Size", "log_cap_june": "Size FF", "beta": "Beta"}))
```

## The Size Factor

SMB is the average of three small-stock portfolios less the average of
three big-stock portfolios. The three portfolios in each size group
cover low, middle, and high book-to-market. Using the same book-to-market
groups on both sides reduces the factor's exposure to the value spread.

For the historical factor series we use the monthly Fama–French SMB
from July 1926 through December 2012.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem9-smb
#| fig-cap: Cumulative returns on the Fama–French SMB factor (BEM Figure 9.2)
#| echo: false
from _bem_monthly import plot_factor

plot_factor("smb")
```
